title: Payments Platform Weekly Sync – Kafka Lag, PgBouncer Migration, Support Bot Fine-tuning
summary: The team reviewed three agenda items: a Kafka consumer lag incident, the upcoming PgBouncer migration, and the support‑bot fine‑tuning experiment. Rohan confirmed the incident was resolved and will add a Grafana alert for consumer lag by Thursday. The group decided to roll out PgBouncer to production in the next sprint and to write a rollout runbook, while the idempotency key fix will be scheduled later. Kabir will gather GPU cost comparisons for serving the bot, and the decision on using VLLM will be revisited in a future meeting.

points: The settlements topic consumer lag spiked above 40,000 messages on Tuesday.
Root cause was a bad Redis connection pool setting introduced in the recent deploy.
P99 latency on the webhook endpoint rose to 1,200 ms; the config was rolled back and lag returned to normal.
There is currently no Grafana alert for consumer lag.
PgBouncer in transaction‑pooling mode reduced connection count by 60% on staging.
The team agreed to move PgBouncer to production in the next sprint.
A rollout runbook will be written.
Idempotency‑key handling in the Razorpay webhook needs fixing but will be scheduled later.
A Llama model was fine‑tuned on 8,000 support tickets, improving accuracy from 71% to 78%.
The model is not yet production‑ready.
The team discussed serving the model with VLLM to reduce GPU cost but postponed the decision.
Kabir will collect GPU cost numbers for both serving options before the next sync.
